questions.question: Scope, and how to settle BUG-333? I tested on 3.13 and every native writer refuses a strided memoryview with BufferError: SpooledTemporaryFile, BytesIO, and open('wb') (which is LocalBackend's open_atomic stream). v0.33.0's MemoryBackend yielded a BytesIO. Only the kernel's _HandleStream, which is unreleased, accepts one.

options.label: All four; narrow BUG-333 (Recommended)
options.description: Fix BUG-329/330/331 and make _HandleStream refuse a non-contiguous buffer the way Python's files do. One small change makes every open_atomic agree and restores v0.33.0's Memory behaviour. Nothing is filed.

options.label: All four; widen BUG-333
options.description: Wrap every open_atomic stream (kernel spool, adapter spool, S3 ×3, Azure, plus Local/SFTP files) so that write and writelines copy any buffer. Much wider diff, and SFTP can't be tested without Docker.

options.label: Three; file BUG-333 out
options.description: Ship BUG-329/330/331 and leave BUG-333 open with the measurement added to it.

questions.question: BUG-329: where should metadata that isn't a mapping (5, [('k','v')], 'ab') be refused, and with what?

options.label: Kernel + Store, ValueError (Recommended)
options.description: Store's _validate_metadata and the kernel's gate both refuse any non-None value that isn't a Mapping, ahead of the capability check (WR-011's shape-first order). ValueError matches WR-011's 'violations raise ValueError' and Store's existing non-str-key error. The kernel refuses before put, so folder d is never created.

options.label: Kernel + Store, TypeError
options.description: Same placement. TypeError is the more idiomatic Python error and matches the kernel's content refusal, but it departs from WR-011's single error type.

options.label: Kernel only
options.description: Store keeps failing with AttributeError from .items(), which today blocks all of these values by accident.

questions.question: BUG-331: how should an unsized read() on a non-blocking stream stop truncating?

options.label: Sized reads in the proxy (Recommended)
options.description: The kernel's stream proxy turns read() / read(-1) / readall() into a loop of read(256 KiB), checking each chunk, so a None is refused whatever the driver does. The guide's 'Read it in full' snippet stays correct. Line reads (readline, iteration) remain a stated bound in BE-030.

options.label: Change the guide and the fake
options.description: Teach drivers to read in sized chunks, and fix tests/_kernel/_fake.py. The kernel's guarantee stays limited to drivers that follow the guide.

answers.BUG-331: how should an unsized read() on: waht is the long term best solution? safe, relaible & performant? a guide follows that, not solution follows guide

questions.question: BUG-331: how should an unsized read() on a non-blocking stream stop truncating?

answers.BUG-331: how should an unsized read() on: waht is the long term best solution? safe, relaible & performant? a guide follows that, not solution follows guide

questions.question: BUG-331, long term: put the guarantee in the kernel, not in each driver. The proxy turns read(), read(-1), read(None) and readall() into a loop of checked read(256 KiB) calls. Safe: a None is refused whatever any driver does, now or later. Reliable: the proxy still forwards every other attribute of the caller's stream (seek, tell, name, with, iteration), which ASYNC-091's tests pin. Performance: the same as today, because a raw readall already loops and joins, so it costs one join and no extra copy. The guide then needs no change, and a driver that reads in full is correct. One bound remains: readline, readlines and iteration loop inside the caller's own object, where no proxy can intercept them. How should line reads be handled?

options.label: State them as BE-030's bound (Recommended)
options.description: Proxy fix for read/readall. BE-030 keeps one narrow sentence saying line reads on a raw non-blocking stream are not covered. No driver reads binary content line by line: Memory uses read(65536), the guide uses read().

options.label: Also refuse line reads on raw streams
options.description: For an io.RawIOBase content stream, the proxy refuses readline/readlines/iteration with a marked TypeError. That closes the bound, but it rejects a legitimate use on blocking raw streams (FileIO), which today work.

options.label: Replace the proxy with a kernel reader
options.description: Hand drivers a kernel-owned BufferedReader over a checked readinto, so every read method derives from one checked primitive. Fully closed, but drivers lose seek/tell/name on the caller's stream, which breaks ASYNC-091's pinned forwarding and any driver that probes size by seeking.
